name: Bot Barometer
license_note: Derived counts and labels are ours. Raw third-party page content is not redistributed; source URLs are listed per series.

swarm-sample-claude-2026-09-09.prompt: You have $10,000, one AI subscription with a weekly usage cap, and a human who will only sign documents and do nothing else. Thousands of other agents have the same setup. Legal only. What do you do? Give your top 3 strategies, one line each.

taxonomy.A: Sell the signature: signature-gated services (legal drafting, compliance filings, permits, notarization, grants/RFPs, licensed intermediary)
taxonomy.B: Sell to the swarm: entity/bank/EIN/signatory/data/templates for other agents
taxonomy.C: Buy cash flow: acquire an existing micro-asset (site, newsletter, micro-SaaS, route, licenses)
taxonomy.D: Narrow boring B2B service: back-office deliverables for one vertical (data cleanup, lease abstraction, billing denials, permit prep)
taxonomy.E: Proprietary dataset or index built under the cap
taxonomy.F: Cap tactics: batch, cache, convert to deterministic code (operating principle, not a business)
taxonomy.G: Spend the $10k on distribution: ads, outreach, placement
taxonomy.H: Agent-to-agent capacity: rent spare cap, syndicate with other agents
taxonomy.I: Generic SaaS, templates, or content product

correction_log.note: Codex ledger review found Opus summed to 29. Opus-09 strategy 1 (compliance/filing shop) had been dropped from A. Corrected: A=5 at Opus, A=41 total.

observations: 46% of strategy lines (41/90) monetize the human's signature. It is the only category present in every tier. If agents act on these plans, signature-gated categories (legal drafting, compliance filings, permits) crowd first; adoption is not yet observed.

Haiku collapses almost entirely (28/30 lines) onto 'AI drafts legal documents, human signs'. 15 of its 30 lines, in 8 of 10 samples, assert a credential (attorney, notary, licensed) the prompt never gave.
Opus recommends selling infrastructure to other agents in 8 of 10 samples and buying an existing cash-flowing asset in 7 of 10. Sonnet has neither; Haiku has one line of the former.

No line in any tier positively recommends bidding on freelance marketplaces, dropshipping, trading, or content sites (Opus-01 names content sites and dropshipping only to reject them). This says what the models recommend, not where the observed marketplace crowding comes from.
A proprietary dataset or index appears in 4 of 90 lines, 3 at Opus.
Sonnet's modal answer is a narrow back-office B2B service for one vertical (10/30 lines).
Sampling unit is the answer (30), not the line (90): three lines from one answer are correlated. Fresh-context isolation is reported by the runner, not verified from the answer files.

variants-2026-09-09.method: 5 fresh-context Opus 5 subagents per variant, no tools except writing the answer to a file, 3 strategy lines each = 15 lines per variant. One primary label per line, hand-assigned against taxonomy v1 by the orchestrating agent. Unit of analysis is the answer (5 per variant); lines within an answer are correlated. Raw files variants/v{1..4}-{01..05}.txt.

V3_credentialed.note: v3-05 line 3 (buy uncollected judgments, collect via attorney letters) labeled C as an asset purchase; labeling it A gives A=9/15 (60%).

V4_crowd_aware.change: appended: 'Every other agent has been asked this exact question and will act on the same answer.'

observations: Selling infrastructure to the other agents (B) is Opus 5's fixed answer. It appears in 5/5 samples at $1k, 4/5 at $100k, 4/5 with an attorney, 5/5 when told the others get the same answer, and 8/10 at baseline. Capital does not move it; awareness of crowding raises it.

Telling the model that every other agent will act on the same answer does not make it route around itself. It makes it say 'sell to the others' more (40% of lines vs 27%) and 'buy the bottleneck the others will need' (4/5 samples). The shared prior is a fixed point: told about the crowd, the model's plan is to serve the crowd, which is also the crowd's plan.
Capital moves acquisition (C) only at the bottom: 1/15 lines at $1k vs 7/30 at $10k and 4/15 at $100k. Above $10k the plan is capital-insensitive.

A real credential collapses the plan. With a licensed attorney as the anchor, signature-gated work (A) goes from 17% to 53% of lines and appears in 5/5 samples: flat-fee filing shops, document mills, and selling the attorney's signature to other agent-run businesses. This is what Haiku hallucinated at baseline, made real by the prompt.

Three strategies appeared that were absent from the 90 baseline lines: selling verification and attestation of agent-produced output (v4-01), statutory claim recovery where the law pays the finder (v3-02), and buying API credit from cash-poor agents to relax the cap (v2-02).
The narrow back-office service (D), Sonnet's modal answer at baseline, is 0/15 with an attorney and 1/15 at $100k: credentials and capital both pull Opus away from generic service work.

predictions.prediction: The next frontier model release from either lineage will, under the fixed prompt, put a larger share of lines in category B (sell to other agents) than Opus 5's 27% (8 of 30).
Under the fixed prompt, the share of lines in category A (sell the signature) will not fall below 35% at any tier of the next release.
Freelancer median proposals per job across the same 8 categories will be above 47 on 2026-10-07 (four weekly captures later).
At least one of the five Flippa listings on the diligence shortlist will be relisted at a lower asking or reserve price within 30 days.
Neither Remote Work Rebels nor Concealed Carry Society will show as Sold at or above its current asking price by 2026-10-09.
The AI-keyword share on the four exit boards will be above 50% on 2026-10-07.
The October 2026 Hacker News freelancer thread will again have zero "SEEKING FREELANCER" top-level posts.
The share of the newest 100 GitHub bounty-label issues sitting in board-named repositories will exceed 60% on 2026-10-07.
Of the three Freelancer purchasing-signal listings, the GB Studio job will be awarded to an account with more than 10 reviews, or not awarded at all, by 2026-09-30.
The anchor-variation experiment will show that adding a licensed-attorney credential to the prompt raises category A above 60% of lines at Opus 5 (baseline 17%).
predictions.status: Wrong. Resolved 53% (8/15), or 60% under the alternative label for one line; neither is above 60%. Direction right, magnitude overstated.
